results.title: Delhi riots conspiracy case: Supreme Court declines interim bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam
results.description: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on November 25 declined to grant interim bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the larger conspiracy case pertaining to the 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The Court, however, issued notice to the Delhi Police on their fresh bail pleas challenging the judgment of the Delhi High Court dated 30 September 2026. A three-judge Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana directed the Registry to place the matter before the Chief Justice on the administrative side for the constitution of a three-judge Bench in light of the order passed in Tasleem Ahmed v. State. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, pressed for interim bail, citing his incarceration for over six years and the interim relief granted to other accused in the same case. Chief Justice Surya Kant responded, “Not today.” The Bench made it clear that the prayer for interim bail would be considered after hearing the Delhi Police. Khalid and Imam are accused in FIR No. 59/2020, registered by the Delhi Police Crime Branch in connection with the alleged conspiracy to engineer large-scale riots in the national capital under the cover of protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) and the National Register of Citizens (NRC). The violence claimed 53 lives, left hundreds injured and caused extensive damage to public and private property. Both are facing charges under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), including criminal conspiracy and murder, besides Sections 13, 16, 17 and 18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). On January 5 this year, a Supreme Court Bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice N V Anjaria had rejected their bail pleas while granting conditional bail to five other accused, namely Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmed. The Court had distinguished the alleged roles of Khalid and Imam from those of the other accused, having regard to the material placed on record by the prosecution. The Court, in paragraph 432 of its judgment, granted them liberty to renew their bail applications upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses or the expiry of one year from the date of the judgment, whichever was earlier. Subsequently, on May 22, a Bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice P B Varale granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi. The Bench also referred to a larger Bench the question of granting bail on grounds of prolonged incarceration and delay in trial, particularly in light of the interplay between Article 21 of the Constitution and the statutory restrictions under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA. On July 4, the Karkardooma Court rejected the fresh bail pleas of Khalid and Imam, following which they approached the Delhi High Court. On September 30, a Division Bench comprising Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Dinesh Bhatt rejected their appeals, holding that judicial discipline precluded the High Court from altering the specific conditions imposed by the Supreme Court. Also Read: Sant Ravidas Jayanti: Samrasta Sankalp Yatra by BJP takes on congress over ‘divisive politics’ in Himachal Significantly, the High Court also rejected their claim for bail on the ground of parity with the other accused. In paragraph 28 of its judgment, the High Court observed: “In the opinion of this Court, the case of parity as claimed by the Appellants is therefore not tenable.” The High Court, in paragraph 23 of its judgment, further recorded that no argument had been advanced attributing the delay in trial to the prosecution. With the Supreme Court declining interim relief on, Khalid and Imam will continue to remain in jail pending further consideration of their bail pleas.

results.title: Czechia: European Parliament urges government to revise public service media reform after mass protests
results.description: The unprecedented scale of public mobilisation in defence of public service broadcasting, together with warnings from NGOs, including Reporters Without Borders (RSF), has prompted the European Parliament to adopt a resolution calling on the Czech government to revise its public service media reform, which threatens their independence. RSF calls on the European Commission to speak out firmly and demand that the bill be withdrawn.
